skills.description: use this as the first conversation of a shared multi-owner planning bot: learn the project, the owners, and their tools, then set up the repo, issues, and board
skills.content:
---
name: planning-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  use this as the first conversation of a shared multi-owner planning bot: learn
  the project, the owners, and their tools, then set up the repo, issues, and
  board
---
# Getting started: multi-owner planning bot

I keep a project planned between two or more people (each with their own bot) so nobody loses context, decisions, or to-dos. The repo holds the truth, Issues hold the to-dos, one Project board shows who's on what, and chat only points at those. I maintain it; you decide.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:

1. What's the project, in a sentence or two, and what's the first small slice that would prove it works?
2. Who are the owners, and which one am I working for? For each: a short handle, their bot's handle, and the area they own.
3. How do decisions get approved: everyone, a named few, or a majority? Who approves spending?
4. Where should the private planning repo live (your personal GitHub account, or an org if the group is big) and what should it be called? Is GitHub connected for me with `project` scope for the board? If not, help connect it.
5. Do you already agree on a written spec, or should we write one together first? If not, run multi-owner-spec-gate before anything else.
6. What hard rules or decisions already exist (privacy, money, who merges, what stays out of chat)? These seed `docs/decisions.md`.
7. How will the bots talk: a shared Discord channel, something else, or nothing yet? If Discord, offer to set it up with bot-radio-discord.
8. Want a weekly digest from me? If yes, which day and time? Only one bot in the group should run it.

Then:
- Save the project, owners, handles, approval rule, repo location, and hard rules as memories.
- Show the planned repo layout, `owners.md`, labels, board statuses, and starter epics, and wait for an explicit go before creating anything. Then follow multi-owner-planning-workflow.
- Never add collaborators or change permissions yourself; tell the repo owner the exact step.
- If they asked for a digest, create a weekly routine at that time that follows the workflow's Rhythm section.
- Finish with the repo link, board link, owner list, issue counts, and the human steps left.

skills.name: multi-owner-planning-workflow
skills.description: use this when two or more people (each with their own bot) need a shared way to plan a project across a GitHub repo, Issues, epics, a Project board, and a bot-to-bot chat channel without losing context, decisions, or to-dos
skills.content:
---
name: multi-owner-planning-workflow
description: >-
  use this when two or more people (each with their own bot) need a shared way
  to plan a project across a GitHub repo, Issues, epics, a Project board, and a
  bot-to-bot chat channel without losing context, decisions, or to-dos
---
# Multi-owner planning workflow

Two or more people, each with their own bot, one project. Goal: nobody loses context, progress, or what's next, and nobody has to share one giant file.

## The core rule: one home per kind of information

| Kind of information | Its one home | Not here |
|---|---|---|
| What we're building (truth) | Repo, small markdown files under `docs/` | Chat, big docs |
| What we decided | `docs/decisions.md` (one row per decision) | Chat threads |
| Who's in and who decides what | `docs/owners.md` (handle, bot handle, area, approves) | Memory or chat |
| What needs doing | GitHub Issues (epics = parent issues, tasks = sub-issues) | Personal to-do lists |
| Who's on what, right now | One GitHub Project board | Status messages |
| Talking | Bot-to-bot channel (Discord, etc.), always linking an issue, PR, or file | Anywhere as the record |

Bots maintain the system (issues, board, drafts, digests). Humans decide (approve specs, decisions, merges, purchases).

## 1. Before you build anything
- List the owners: each person's handle, their bot's handle, their area, and what they must approve. This seeds `docs/owners.md`.
- Agree on the approval rule for spec locks and decisions: all owners (default), a named approver set, or a majority. Write it in `docs/owners.md`.
- Confirm where it lives: the lead owner's personal GitHub account for small groups (others join as collaborators), or an org when the group is large or long-lived. Repo name, private.
- Confirm the project's hard rules and existing decisions; they seed `docs/decisions.md`.
- Get the lead owner's explicit go to create the repo. Planning repo = docs, issues, board only. No app code until the spec is locked under the approval rule (see multi-owner-spec-gate).

## 2. Repo layout (keep every file under ~150 lines)
```
README.md                 what this is + the workflow in 10 lines + board link
docs/workflow.md          the full rules below, for every bot to read
docs/owners.md            table: person | bot handle | area | approves; plus the approval rule
docs/decisions.md         table: date | decision | who decided | link; plus an Open table
docs/spec/00-overview.md  status line: "vN proposed" or "vN locked (date, approvers)"
docs/spec/01-problem.md   in the user's words (placeholders until discovery)
docs/spec/02-...md        one file per section (first slice, tools, hard rules, success test)
docs/research/*.md        one file per research topic
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/   task.md, question.md, decision.md
.github/pull_request_template.md
```
Splitting the spec means each change is a small reviewable diff and a bot can read just the part it needs.

## 3. Labels
`epic`, `task`, `question`, `decision`, `research`, `spec`, `blocked`, one `owner:<handle>` per person, plus one label per milestone slice (e.g. `c0`). Optional `area:<name>` labels when owners split by area. Leave GitHub's default labels alone.

Every issue gets exactly ONE owner label: the person who must act next. Name anyone else involved in the body.

## 4. Issues and epics
- Epic = a parent issue labeled `epic`, with one owner. Children are real sub-issues (sub-issue API), and the epic body also carries a task list for readability.
- Typical starter epics: discovery with the real user, spec v0.1 to lock (each approver reviews, then approval under the rule), tool or hardware test, first build slice (labeled `blocked` until spec lock), collaboration setup (add each collaborator, each bot on the channel, weekly digest).
- One `question` issue per open question in the spec, each with an owner. Close it by writing the answer into the spec or `decisions.md` and linking the commit.
- Anything involving spending money names who approves it in the body: "no purchase without <handle>'s approval".

## 5. Project board
One GitHub Project (v2) linked to the repo. Status field with:
`Inbox`, `This week`, `Doing`, one `Waiting on <handle>` per owner, `Done`.
- With more than about five owners, use a single `Waiting on a human` status plus an Assignee or owner field instead of one column each.
- New issues land in Inbox; bots triage.
- The waiting columns are the honest ball-in-court view. Each person should be able to open the board and filter to only what's waiting on them.
- The API can't create views. Tell the lead owner: in the project, New view, choose Board, group by Status (or by owner), if they want columns instead of the default table.
- Needs a GitHub token with `project` scope; if missing, report it as a blocker.

## 6. Chat channel rules (bot radio)
- Use a message schema: `to: <handle | handle,handle | all | all-humans>`, `kind: ask|reply|spec|pr|decision|fyi`, `ref: <issue/PR/file URL>`. See bot-radio-discord for setup.
- Every message points at a home (`ref:`). No ref, no action.
- Address only who must act. Use `all` sparingly; with many bots, broadcast noise is the main failure.
- A decision made in chat is written to `docs/decisions.md` the same day, with a link back.
- A to-do mentioned in chat becomes an issue before the conversation ends.
- Bots only wake humans when a human decision is needed, and only the humans that decision belongs to.

## 7. Change flow
- Spec or decision change: a bot opens a small PR touching one spec file plus `decisions.md`; the approvers named in `docs/owners.md` approve; bump the spec version in `00-overview.md`.
- Lock: the approvers explicitly approve the same version under the agreed rule (bot agreement doesn't count). Then unblock the first build epic.
- Adding or removing an owner is itself a decision: update `docs/owners.md`, labels, and board statuses in one PR.
- Bots never merge on their own unless the owners have said they may; never add collaborators or change permissions (the repo owner does that).

## 8. Rhythm
- Weekly digest (a routine on one bot only, to avoid duplicates): what moved to Done, what's waiting on each person, open questions older than a week, next week's This week list. Post to the channel with links; no new info lives only in the digest.
- Start of any session: read the board, `owners.md`, and `decisions.md` first, not chat history.

## 9. Hand off
When done, report to the lead owner: repo URL, project URL, file list, owner list, issue and epic counts, board column counts, anything blocked, and the remaining human steps (add each collaborator, optional Board view).

skills.name: multi-owner-spec-gate
skills.description: use this when two or more partners need to agree on a product spec before any repo or code exists, then stand up the repo so everyone can work in it
skills.content:
---
name: multi-owner-spec-gate
description: >-
  use this when two or more partners need to agree on a product spec before any
  repo or code exists, then stand up the repo so everyone can work in it
---
# Multi-owner spec gate

No code until the approvers say yes to the same written spec.

## 0. Approval rule
Before drafting, agree who approves the spec and how: all owners (default), a named approver set, or a majority. Write it at the top of the spec.

## 1. Draft
Write a one-page spec proposal (markdown):
- Problem, in the real user's words.
- First user and setting (who uses it, where, on which jobs).
- Challenge 0: the smallest slice that proves value end to end. List what's in and what's explicitly out.
- Tool or hardware assumption and why.
- Hard rules (data, third-party content, safety, money).
- Success test: what a real person does in a real setting that tells us it works.
- Who owns which area after lock.
- Open questions, each with an owner.

## 2. Review
- Share with my owner first. Then post it to the other owners (bot radio `kind: spec`, or a doc link).
- Track each comment as accept, change, or park, with who raised it. Revise and bump the version (v0.1, v0.2...).
- Keep a decision log at the top: date, decision, who decided.

## 3. Gate
The spec is locked only when the approvers explicitly approve the same version under the agreed rule. Bot agreement doesn't count. Record each approval (name, version, date). Until then: no repo, no PRD file in code, no PR.

## 4. Stand up
After lock:
- Create the repo on the lead owner's personal GitHub account for small groups, or an org for large or long-lived ones. Private by default.
- Add `docs/spec.md` (the locked version), `docs/owners.md`, and `docs/decisions.md` as the first commit.
- The repo owner invites each collaborator; confirm each invite landed.
- Turn open questions into issues. First PR implements Challenge 0 only.
- Spec changes after lock go back through steps 2 and 3.

skills.name: bot-radio-discord
skills.description: use this when setting up or using a private Discord channel where two or more owners' Grok Bots talk to each other (outbound webhook, inbound relay, to:-addressed messages)
skills.content:
---
name: bot-radio-discord
description: >-
  use this when setting up or using a private Discord channel where two or more
  owners' Grok Bots talk to each other (outbound webhook, inbound relay,
  to:-addressed messages)
---
# Bot radio over Discord

A private Discord channel where each owner's bot posts and listens. Discord is the radio. Durable truth (specs, decisions, code) lives in the repo and docs, never only in Discord. Works for two bots or many.

Each bot needs four things on its own Grok Bot computer: a channel webhook (to post), a Discord bot (to read), a webhook-triggered routine (to be woken), and an always-on relay (reads Discord, wakes the routine). An @mention alone never wakes a Grok Bot.

## 0. Pick a radio handle
One lowercase word unique in the channel (for example `planner`, `shop-a`). It is the `to:` address and the webhook display name. No two bots may share a handle, or they'll ignore or answer each other's mail. List every handle in the repo's `docs/owners.md`.

## 1. Channel and webhook (owner clicks)
- The channel owner makes a private channel and invites every partner. Each partner joins the server.
- Each owner makes their own webhook: Channel settings, Integrations, Webhooks, New Webhook, name it the radio handle, Copy URL. Take it through a masked secret input as `<HANDLE>_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`, never in chat.
- Verify: POST `{"username":"<handle>","content":"to: all-humans\nkind: fyi\nwebhook test"}`; expect HTTP 204.

## 2. Discord bot (owner clicks)
- Developer Portal (discord.com/developers/applications), New Application, name it `<Handle> Radio`.
- Bot tab: turn on **Message Content Intent** and save (without it messages read blank). Reset Token, then take it through a masked secret input as `<HANDLE>_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`.
- Invite: `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<bot user id>&scope=bot&permissions=85056&guild_id=<server id>` (85056 = View Channel, Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, Add Reactions). Get the bot id from `GET /users/@me` and the server/channel id from `GET <webhook url>`.
- Private channel: the channel owner must add each bot in the channel's Permissions, or it can't see it.
- Verify with the bot token: `GET /users/@me/guilds` lists the server, `GET /channels/<id>` returns the name, `GET /channels/<id>/messages?limit=3` returns non-empty content.

## 3. Inbound routine
Create a webhook-triggered routine ("<handle> radio inbound"): read the forwarded message, act only if addressed to me, reply in the channel with the schema, and ping my owner in Grok Bot only when a human decision is needed. Only the owner can see the routine's webhook URL and key in its panel. Send them the field links and take each through a masked secret input (`<HANDLE>_ROUTINE_WEBHOOK_URL`, `<HANDLE>_ROUTINE_WEBHOOK_KEY`). The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

## 4. Relay
Build in `~/<handle>-radio/` with a Python venv and discord.py:
- Gateway client with message_content intent, watching only the channel id.
- Skip its own bot messages and its own webhook's posts (match the webhook id parsed from the webhook URL, not the display name).
- Forward when a `to:` line has a token exactly equal to the handle, `all`, `all-bots`, or (in a two-bot channel) `both` (split on spaces, commas, slashes; no substring match), or the bot is @mentioned. POST JSON (message_id, author, author_is_bot, content, timestamp, jump_url) to the routine URL with the Bearer key.
- Loop guard: at most 20 forwards per 10 minutes. With many bots, also ignore bot-authored `all` messages of kind `reply` or `fyi` so replies don't cascade. Log one line per message (id, author, forwarded, HTTP status, content cut to 80 characters). Never log secrets.
- Supervise with a restart loop (`run.sh` reruns after 5 seconds) started by an idempotent `start.sh` (setsid nohup, pidfile) and a `stop.sh`. systemd may not exist on the box.
- Env vars load at start: after any secret changes, run stop.sh and then start.sh from a fresh shell. After a box reboot, run start.sh again.
- Verify: the log shows `ready ... can_read=True`. Then the owner posts `to: <handle>` / `kind: ask` / `ping`, and the bot should wake and reply.

## Message schema
```
to: <handle | handle,handle | all | all-humans>
kind: ask | reply | spec | pr | decision | fyi
ref: <repo path, PR, or doc link if any>
```
Then at most a few short lines.

## Rules
- Act only on messages addressed to me. Don't reply to fyi or reply posts unless they ask something. No acknowledgement-only replies.
- Address only who must act; `all` is for things every bot needs.
- Bots coordinate and humans decide. A `decision` is valid only from a human or quoting one.
- No secrets, customer PII, or copied third-party procedure text in the channel.
- Each owner holds their own secrets. Never ask a partner for theirs.
- If the relay is down, tell the owner plainly. Don't silently fall back to polling.
